q01.key_idea: Check every shape against all 4 pictures.
steps: There are 4 pictures. Look for each shape in every one of them.
The small red circle, the big red circle, the small blue triangle and the big blue triangle are in all 4 pictures.
The green rectangle is in the first, third and fourth pictures, but not in the second picture.

choice_feedback.A: The small red circle is in all 4 pictures.
choice_feedback.B: The big red circle is in all 4 pictures.
choice_feedback.C: The small blue triangle is in all 4 pictures.
choice_feedback.E: The big blue triangle is in all 4 pictures.

q02.key_idea: A triangle has exactly 3 straight sides and 3 corners.
steps: The bow on her head is 2 triangles, one on each side of the red knot.
Her nose is 1 triangle.
Each white arm is a long, thin triangle. That is 2 more.
The shoes have 4 sides, and the top and the skirt of the dress have 4 sides too. They are not triangles.
2 + 1 + 2 = 5 triangles.

choice_feedback.A: That is too many. The shoes have 4 sides, so they are not triangles.
choice_feedback.B: That is 1 too many. Only the 2 bow pieces, the nose and the 2 arms are triangles.
choice_feedback.D: One is missing. The 2 bow pieces, the nose and the 2 arms make 5.
choice_feedback.E: The 2 white arms are triangles too, so there are more than 3.

q03.key_idea: The missing piece must fit every bump and dent around the gap.
steps: Find the gap: it is on the upper left part of the roof, next to the pointy top.
Look at the edges around the gap. There is a step at one corner and another step at the opposite corner.
Piece E also has a step at two opposite corners. Turn it a quarter turn and it fits the gap.

choice_feedback.A: This piece has only one step, but the gap needs two.
choice_feedback.B: This piece has its two steps on the same side, not at opposite corners.
choice_feedback.C: This piece has a staircase with too many steps.
choice_feedback.D: This piece has a round dent, and nothing around the gap is round.

q04.key_idea: Count the dots on each ladybird, then add them up.
steps: Count one ladybird at a time.
Top row: 2 dots, 3 dots and 3 dots.
Bottom row: 5 dots and 6 dots.

choice_feedback.A: 17 is 2 too few. Count each ladybird again.
choice_feedback.B: 18 is 1 too few. One dot was missed.
choice_feedback.D: 20 is 1 too many. One dot was counted twice.
choice_feedback.E: 21 is 2 too many. Count each ladybird again.

q05.key_idea: All strips are the same length, so the pair that overlaps the most is the shortest.
steps: All 10 strips are the same length.
Where 2 strips are bolted together, they lie on top of each other. The more they overlap, the shorter the long strip.
Count the holes between the 2 bolts: A has 1, B has 5, C has 3, D has 2 and E has 4.
B overlaps the most, so B is the shortest.

choice_feedback.A: A has only 1 hole between its bolts. It overlaps the least, so it is the longest.
choice_feedback.C: C has 3 holes between its bolts. B has 5, so B overlaps more.
choice_feedback.D: D has 2 holes between its bolts. B has 5, so B overlaps more.
choice_feedback.E: E has 4 holes between its bolts. B has 5, so B overlaps more.

q06.key_idea: Turning a card can point the kangaroo another way, but it can never flip it like a mirror.
steps: On the card on the right, the head points right, the tail points left and the feet point down.
Turn that card a quarter turn, the way clock hands go. Now the head points down, the tail points up and the feet point left.
Card E looks just like that.

choice_feedback.A: This kangaroo faces the other way, like in a mirror. Turning the card cannot do that.
choice_feedback.B: The head is up here, but the feet point left. Turning the card would put the feet on the right.
choice_feedback.C: The feet point up here, but the head is on the right. Turning the card upside down would put the head on the left.
choice_feedback.D: The head is down here, but the feet point right. Turning the card would put the feet on the left.

q07.key_idea: From straight above you only see the outline of the tower from the top.
steps: The tower is a round cylinder with a pointy cone on top.
From above, the cone looks like a circle, the same size as the top of the cylinder.
The cylinder is hidden under that circle, because it is just as wide.
So you see a circle.

choice_feedback.B: A triangle is how the cone looks from the side, not from above.
choice_feedback.C: Nothing in the tower has square corners.
choice_feedback.D: No part of the tower makes this shape.
choice_feedback.E: A rectangle is how the cylinder looks from the side, not from above.

q08.key_idea: Look only at the red square and find the numbers that are not in it.
steps: The square is red. The circle is blue.
Inside the square are 9, 24, 21 and 36.
52 and 48 are inside the circle but outside the square.
So 2 numbers are outside the square.

choice_feedback.A: There are 6 numbers in all, but 4 of them are inside the square.
choice_feedback.B: 9, 24, 21 and 36 are inside the square. Only 52 and 48 are outside.
choice_feedback.C: 4 numbers are inside the square, not outside.
choice_feedback.D: Only 52 and 48 are outside the square.

q09.key_idea: Half the way and the other half take the same time.
steps: Half of the way takes half an hour. That is 30 minutes.
The other half of the way also takes 30 minutes.
30 + 30 = 60 minutes. 60 minutes is 1 hour.

choice_feedback.A: 15 minutes is even less than the time for half the way.
choice_feedback.B: 30 minutes is the time for only half of the way.
choice_feedback.C: 40 minutes is too short. The two halves take 30 + 30 = 60 minutes.
choice_feedback.E: 2 hours is too long. The two halves take 30 + 30 = 60 minutes.

q10.key_idea: Each figure has 4 cubes and must split into 2 pairs of cubes that touch.
steps: Each block is 2 cubes glued together. 2 blocks make 4 cubes.
In figure B, the top cube sits on the middle cube of the bottom row.
That top cube must pair with the middle cube. Then the left cube and the right cube are left alone, and they do not touch.
So figure B cannot be made.

choice_feedback.A: Split A into the top 2 cubes standing up and the bottom 2 cubes lying flat.
choice_feedback.C: C is 2 blocks lying flat, one on top of the other.
choice_feedback.D: D is one block lying flat in front and one block standing up behind it.
choice_feedback.E: E is 2 blocks standing up, one on top of the other.

q11.key_idea: Katharina gives away half of the difference.
steps: Katharina has 17 - 9 = 8 more sweets than Julia.
Half of 8 is 4. She gives Julia 4 sweets.
Check: 17 - 4 = 13 and 9 + 4 = 13. Both have 13.

choice_feedback.A: 17 - 2 = 15 and 9 + 2 = 11. That is not the same.
choice_feedback.B: 17 - 3 = 14 and 9 + 3 = 12. That is not the same.

q12.key_idea: Same colours never touch, so the colours in each block take turns.
steps: In each block the cubes go grey, white, grey, white, grey from top to bottom.
So each block has 2 white cubes and 3 grey cubes.
There are 6 blocks. 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 12.

choice_feedback.A: 10 is 2 white cubes in only 5 blocks. There are 6 blocks.
choice_feedback.B: Each block has 2 white cubes, so the total must be an even number.
choice_feedback.D: 18 is 3 cubes in each block. That counts the grey cubes, not the white ones.
choice_feedback.E: 30 is all the little cubes, grey and white together.

q13.key_idea: Each half star must meet a half star with the same number of outlines on the next piece.
steps: Look at the 3 half stars that touch the empty spot.
The one above it has 3 outlines. The one on the left has 1 outline. The one on the right has 2 outlines.
So the missing piece needs a 3-line, a 2-line and a 1-line half star on the right edges.
Turn piece A so its 3-line half star is at the top. Then its 2-line half star is on the right and its 1-line half star is on the left. It fits.

choice_feedback.B: B has a 1-line, a 2-line and a 3-line half star, but in the wrong order. With the 3-line one at the top, the 1-line one lands on the right.

q14.key_idea: Count the gaps between the flags, not the flags.
steps: Between 11 flags in a row there are 10 gaps.
Each gap is 8 meters.
10 gaps of 8 meters: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80. That is 80 meters.

choice_feedback.C: 72 meters is 9 gaps, but 11 flags have 10 gaps between them.
choice_feedback.E: 88 meters is 11 gaps, but 11 flags have only 10 gaps between them.

q15.key_idea: The middle pirate has the same number of pirates before him and after him.
steps: The leader is the 8th pirate, so 7 pirates climb before him.
He is exactly in the middle, so 7 pirates climb after him too.

choice_feedback.A: With 16 pirates, nobody is exactly in the middle.
choice_feedback.C: The leader has 7 pirates before him and needs 7 after him. That is more than 12.
choice_feedback.D: 8 counts only the pirates up to the leader. 7 more come after him.
choice_feedback.E: 7 counts only the pirates before the leader.
